name: James Aldrich
bio: James Aldrich (1810–1856) was an American poet, and has no connection with the better-known Thomas Bailey Aldrich. He is remembered almost entirely for one short poem, “A Death-bed”, widely reprinted in nineteenth-century anthologies.
Little is recorded about his life, and this archive makes no claim beyond his dates and the single poem Knowles printed.

poems.title: A Death-bed
poems.author: James Aldrich
poems.collection: The Golden Treasury of American Songs and Lyrics (1899)
poems.text:
Her suffering ended with the day,
  Yet lived she at its close,
And breathed the long, long night away
  In statue-like repose.

But when the sun in all his state
  Illumed the eastern skies,
She passed through Glory's morning gate
  And walked in Paradise.
